newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates slip in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates slip in thin market.

text.p: Dutch money rates slipped a few basis points on Friday, with dealers saying they could ease further during the early part of this month.

One-month deposits dipped to 2.98 percent bid after hovering just above 3.02 percent last week. Dealers said more players were gradually returning to the market after the Christmas and New Year holiday-break.
The Amsterdam Interbank Offered Rate (AIBOR), closely watched as a market guide, was also down, with one-month AIBOR slipping four basis points to 3.09 percent.

Call money was bid at 2.81 percent versus Thursday's 2.88 percent, with dealers saying that Thursday's central bank allocation of 4.38 billion guilders under an eight-day advances pact was still sufficient.
Dealers noted some buying interest in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) as the rate for February contracts was set at 3.03 for big tranches and 3.02 percent for smaller parcels.
The guilder was barely changed against the mark, trading at 112.235 per 100 marks from 112.23 on Thursday.
